# Project State

## Project Reference

See: .planning/PROJECT.md (updated 2026-07-05)

**Core value:** One launcher that manages your entire game library across Epic, GOG, Amazon, and Steam — without needing to open Steam, Epic, or GOG separately.
**Current focus:** Phase 46 — windows-single-instance-guard-and-gamelib-deep-link-registra

> inflated `v1.x` planning labels to `0.x` to reflect pre-release status (map:
> v1.N → v0.(N+1)). Milestones are now: **v0.1** Steam Platform · **v0.2** Polish ·

> native-install = **v0.7** (this milestone). `package.json` set to 0.7.0.

> # ✅ PHASE 34.4.2 COMPLETE — 2026-08-19. BLOCKING LIVE GATE: **PASS 5/5**.
>
> `34.4.2-LIVE-GATE-RERUN-6.md` PASSED on real macOS hardware — the **first full PASS in this
> phase's history**, on the **ninth gate attempt across eight contracts**. Verdict history:
> **FAIL 0/6 → FAIL → FAIL 5/6 → FAIL 5/6 → FAIL 1/6 → FAIL 0/5 → PASS 5/5.**
>
> | Item | Result |
> |---|---|
> | 1 — sheet presentation + minimize/restore | PASS |
> | 2 — dismissability | PASS |
> | 3(a) — no injected affordance | PASS |
> | 4 — Cmd+V as sole credential route | PASS |
> | 6(a) — Humble disconnect route | PASS |
>
> **Item 6(a) was the only never-measured behaviour in the phase**, unreached across eight prior
> attempts. Its PASS live-discharges F-34.4.2-12's fix `6bad86227` and T-34.4.2-43, and meets
> F-34.4.2-10's taking-condition (storage-clear SUCCESS line fired, not the timeout).
>
> **What made it winnable was DELETING work, not doing more.** D-G4 retired REQ-34.4.2-05 and
> REQ-34.4.2-04's glyph half — a retirement ORDERED on 2026-08-05 when the mechanism was deleted,
> but never actioned, leaving both requirements awaiting a live discharge of code that did not
> exist. That dropped sub-checks 3(b)/3(c) as unfalsifiable; 3(c) alone had justified an entire app
> launch and had never run in eight attempts. D-G5 inherited item 6(b), retiring F-34.4.2-20.
> Five launches collapsed to one.
>
> **All 10/10 REQ-34.4.2 boxes ticked. `34.4.2-VERIFICATION.md` amended IN PLACE to
> `status: passed`** (10/11 truths verified, 1 uncertain by design, 0 failed) — never regenerated,
> because `7e1781fbb` had hand-corrected it.
>
> **Two NEW findings the run produced:** F-34.4.2-25 — a required literal can go stale by
> **BEHAVIOUR**, not just line number (verifying it EXISTS ≠ verifying it FIRES on the route the
> item drives); F-34.4.2-26 — Humble's login has an out-of-band 2FA email round-trip that nearly
> consumed `LOGIN_WATCH_TIMEOUT_MS`.
>
> **Next action:** Phase 34.4.2 needs nothing further. Outstanding elsewhere: the 34.13 UAT gate
> (paused at row 5 of 72, awaiting a USB drive for the multi-library fixture) and Phase 23.2 wave 4.

- Phase 34.14 inserted after Phase 34.13 on 2026-08-16: **Steam platform-row depot signal — distinguish 'no Windows build' from 'metadata not captured'** (URGENT). Promoted out of 34.13's review finding **B-WR-06**, which is **superseded, not fixed as filed** — its symptom was real but its cause was wrong, so shipping its prescribed copy would have asserted something false. Verified at HEAD: `hasSteamWindowsDepot` is `is_windows_native === true` (default-deny, `steamPlatformRow.ts:42` explicitly rejects `!== false`), and `is_windows_native` is only written after a successful `appdetails` fetch (`games.ts:647`, stamped `platformsCaptured: true`) which `getGameInfo()` fires **fire-and-forget** while returning the uncaptured value. So an uncaptured game routes to `readonly-macos` and the Windows entry is **dropped from the picker** (`steamPlatformRow.ts:103`) — the wine option is WITHHELD, not merely unexplained. It cannot self-heal: `gameInfo` has exactly three writers in `InstallGameModal.ts` (`:293`, `:326`, `:336`) and is written **only at open time**, so a fetch landing mid-dialog is never seen; offline or a failed fetch makes it persist. **Operator domain constraint (locked):** mac-only Steam games are effectively a null set, so `readonly-macos` is in practice a synonym for "metadata not loaded yet" — hence scope item (d), write NO mac-only copy. Scope: thread the existing `platformsCaptured` signal into the gating input (precedent: `AppleWikiInfo.tsx:67`), render not-captured as a **pending** row via the D-25 pattern, and weigh refreshing the open snapshot against `closeInstallGameModal`'s recorded stale-cross-game-state hazard. Affects the **"Install with options…" route only** (D-23 short-circuits plain Install). Needs a UAT gate, whose steps must specify how to force an uncaptured state — the cold-cache window is not reproducible on demand from a warm library.
- Phase 34.15 inserted after Phase 34.14 on 2026-08-16: **Steam platform-signal and sync integrity**. Carries the three pre-existing Steam defects 34.14's D-08 UAT gate surfaced but never claimed to fix (the fourth, the pre-D-17 cache residue, was closed by quick task `260816-hdg`). 34.14 made the renderer behave **safely** when the depot signal is missing; 34.15 reduces how often it is missing, gives the sync a terminal failure state, and applies 34.14's own *absent-is-not-negative* principle to the **mac** side, where it was never applied. **(1) HIGH — the sync captures NO platform data**, it only reads the cache (`library.ts:785-787`); `getOwnedApps()` returns appIds and names only, and platform flags come lazily per-game from `appdetails` (`games.ts:647`, persisted `:704`). So `is_windows_native` is `undefined` across most of a ~378-game library, which makes **D-04's fail-open load-bearing in ORDINARY use**, not merely a network-outage net. Direction: bulk `?appids=a,b,c` capture at sync time or a post-sync backfill, rate-limited and resumable — the endpoint is undocumented and rate-limits aggressively, so MEASURE before choosing a batch size. **Hard constraint:** the three-valued contract survives (`undefined`/`false`/`true`); do NOT collapse `undefined → false`, per the rationale at `library.ts:764-776`. **(2) HIGH — the sync spinner has no failure state and hides the WHOLE library.** `Library/index.tsx:1013-1019` clears only when the library populates, `refreshingInTheBackground` defaults `true` (`GlobalState.tsx:295`), `steam.library` starts `[]` — so a refresh FAILURE spins forever while the backend logs `Steam client not ready` (`library.ts:670`) and nothing propagates. This is the **sibling of the already-fixed bug** at `GlobalState.tsx:1508-1515`: that fix made refresh RUN, not FAIL cleanly. The overlay is also unscoped, so an unreachable Steam hid 6 GOG games in live repro. Needs a regression test for refresh **running-and-failing** specifically — existing coverage only proves it appears and clears on success. **(3) MEDIUM — absent `is_mac_native` read as "no Mac build"**, the exact mirror of the conflation 34.14 eliminated for Windows: `InstallModal/index.tsx:165` and `:242` both collapse unknown into false, so a cold cache rendered a confident Windows-only icon row for Terraria (105600), which genuinely ships both. Direction: extend `steamPlatformRow.ts`'s pure resolver with a mac availability triple, SUPPRESS the icon row while unresolved rather than rendering a confident subset, and decide `getDefaultplatform`'s uncaptured case explicitly with a commented rationale. **Hard prohibition:** do NOT loosen to `is_mac_native !== false` — that is the `treatsAbsentAsAvailable` saboteur shape three shipped gates in `steamPlatformRow.test.ts` exist to reject. Depends on 34.14 and on quick task `260816-hdg`'s `steam/metadataCapture.ts` normalization, which item 1 must not regress. **Out of scope by decision:** the 32-bit-mac orphaned-install todo (install-lifecycle, different axis) and the `provisionBottle` CrossOver guard. Blocks nothing; independent of Phase 35.
- Phase 36 added 2026-08-20: **Login-to-Steam crossfade and explicit login-in-flight mitigation**. The Steam sign-in Dialog slides up into position while the login panel (`.loginContentWrapper`) slides up and out, `.loginBackground` staying painted underneath — so the Steam flow becomes an OVERLAY on `/login` instead of a navigation to the sibling route `loginweb/steam` (`App.tsx:236-239`). **The coupled security work is NOT separable:** that navigation's unmount is currently the ENTIRE frontend mitigation for T-34.4.2-39 (spoofing) and T-34.4.2-41 (DoS) — per `loginInFlightUiReachability.test.tsx`, clicking any tile unmounts all six at once, and the tiles' `disabled` prop is wired ONLY to `oldMac` with no login-in-flight state in `Login/index.tsx`. Keeping the panel mounted makes the other five tiles clickable again, so the phase must add explicit in-flight state (disabled + `pointer-events: none` + `inert`), rewrite that test to pin the NEW mechanism (its current prose would otherwise pass while describing something untrue), and update the threat register. Operator approved this threat-model change on 2026-08-20, choosing it over a cheaper sequential handoff because an explicit guard beats an incidental one. Integer phase chosen DELIBERATELY over a 35.x decimal: plan-phase gap-analysis is blind to decimal-phase REQ IDs. Origin: quick task 260820-kq0, whose Dialog work already supplies the 500ms slide-up entrance (`1b7fa0eaa`). Backdrop is NOT the cause of the flat-grey background — MUI's default is rgba(0,0,0,0.5) with no override; nothing is behind the scrim because the Login screen unmounts. This phase fixes that as a side effect.
- Phase 37 added 2026-08-22: **Steam defect cluster — depot decode failure, false-delisted games, and install-error reporting**. Bundles the seven open Steam todos surfaced by the 34.13 UAT gate and the 2026-08-21 install attempts. **All seven re-verified live at HEAD on 2026-08-22 before the phase was written**, per the ledgered lesson that `resolves_phase:` is absent by default so the todo auto-close misses everything — two of them (`decompress.ts`, `aborthandler.ts`) carry adjacent fixes that look like coverage but are commit-dated **2026-07-19**, a month BEFORE the observations, so neither applies. All seven todos are now tagged `resolves_phase: 37` + `planned_as: 37-0N`. **Two plans are gated and must NOT be authored as ordinary fix tasks:** 37-01 (the `Z_DATA_ERROR` decode failure) has a leading hypothesis — a bad depot decryption key — that is explicitly NOT established, and a prior investigation ruled the CDN-auth arc a PHANTOM *for a different symptom*, a verdict that must not be assumed to transfer; run `/gsd-debug` first. 37-07 (the filesystem orphan scan) is the only non-defect item, carries three unsettled design questions, and is the natural split-out if the phase needs narrowing; run `/gsd-discuss-phase 37` first. **Phase-wide constraint:** 37-03 and 37-06 both need to repair state already written into users' caches, and `MigrationSystem` is dead code under Tauri, so both repairs must self-heal at the READ boundary — a new `Migration` would ship as a silent no-op. 37-02 deliberately does NOT depend on 37-01: a decode-stage failure must never be reported as a dropped connection regardless of why decoding failed. Integer phase chosen over a 36.x decimal for the same reason Phase 36 was: plan-phase gap-analysis is blind to decimal-phase REQ IDs. The sibling '22 games never reach the rendered library' todo is NOT tagged — its fix already landed (`51b175d74`) and it stays OPEN pending an operator full-restart confirmation, which 37's live gate folds into 37-01's repro session; note 37-03 explains only **9** of those 22.
- Phase 44 added 2026-09-15: **In-app Winetricks browse UI replacing the search-only panel**. Motivated by operator feedback the same day: the winetricks zenity GUI's categorised checklist is markedly better than our own panel. The architectural call was to rebuild that shape IN-APP rather than lean harder on zenity -- zenity is already a declared-but-optional dependency the code warns about (`src/backend/tools/index.ts:779`, "zenity not installed! Winetricks might fail to install some packages or even open"), so adopting it as the primary UI would promote a soft dependency to a hard one and discard all ten app themes. Rendering work only: the data layer landed in `quick-260915-ajd` (`listAvailable()` now returns `{verb, title, category, cached}` across 567 verbs, up from 370 verb-only strings) and `quick-260915-ajd-fu` made the filter match title as well as verb. Cost of NOT using zenity, measured rather than assumed: only 8 verbs require manual download and cannot be installed unattended (`3dmark03`, `3dmark06`, `fontxplorer`, `foobar2000`, `stalker_pripyat_bench`, `ubisoftconnect`, `unigine_heaven`, `utorrent`) -- all benchmarks and apps, NOT ONE a DLL or font, so none of the `vcrun*`/`dotnet*`/`d3dx9*`/`corefonts` fixes anyone actually opens this panel for. Those 8 route to the retained zenity button. Scope fence carried from measured history: the list region must NOT unmount on install -- that remount is the cause of the dead-button defect fixed in 35-25 (`366e719bb`).

Promoted from todo `2026-08-29-windows-single-instance-guard-and-deep-link-registration.md` now that the operator has a working Windows 11 build machine (Developer Mode on, pre-push hook green via quick 260922-ok3). It is the unblock for quick 260922-nx4, which suppressed install-time `gamelib://` registration on Windows because there was no guard. - [Phase 34.8-10]: Proved the gate genuinely fails, not just green jest — a real temporary literal added to `GameStatus.tsx` made the assertion fail naming the exact file/line/column/text (recorded verbatim in `34.8-10-SUMMARY.md`), then reverted byte-identical and re-ran green
- [Phase 34.8-11]: `meta/machineFillGamelib.ts` built as a pure D-09 contract layer (`collectMissingKeys`/`buildTranslationMemory`/`validateTranslation`/`mergeFill`/`fillLocale`, no fs/network/clock, `now: Date` threaded through) plus a real `createAnthropicTranslator` backend and CLI, wired as `pnpm machine-fill-gamelib`. D-08's bulk-run refusal ordered BEFORE any credential check or network call — proved live by actually running the CLI three times (unset `GAMELIB_MT_LOCALES`, `=all` without `GAMELIB_MT_CONFIRM_BULK=1`, a named locale with no `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`), all three non-zero exit with the correct message, transcripts recorded in `34.8-11-SUMMARY.md`. `git status --porcelain public/locales/` stayed empty across all three runs — deliberately NOT bulk-run this phase (D-08). - **NEW (2026-09-17, major, `ready: live-gate`): the packaged `.app` renders blank on roughly 1 launch in 4 — and it is NOT a boot failure.** Measured on a properly Tauri-signed bundle (`flags=0x10000(runtime)`, `allow-jit`, team `S7U223QWXJ`): blank on launch 1 (luma 238.86, stddev 3.76), correct on the next three launches of the same binary (stddev 77.81 / 77.13 / 77.82). **Signing is disproved as the cause** — it was the first hypothesis and blank renders occur on correctly signed bundles. Three measurements rule out the whole "app didn't boot" class: `bootErrorSurface.ts:62` bails when `root.childElementCount > 0` and the blank page read `#eceff4` (nord-light's own `--background-light`) not its `#141414`, so `#root` HAD children; the blank run's log has `Frontend Ready` with the library refreshed and games found; and WebContent RSS was 58 MB blank-but-mounted vs 429 MB rendered, where a compositor-only drop should have sat near 429. So this is layout/paint, and the deliverable is one discriminating probe, not an investigation: diff `getBoundingClientRect()` for `#root` + two descendant levels between a blank and a rendered launch. Garbage/zero heights implicate the known WKWebView convergence family that was the real cause of F-10's blank Manage Accounts screen — prime suspect `App.css:22-31`, `.App` being `grid-template-rows: min-content min-content 1fr min-content` under `height: 100vh`. **Severity is interim:** only locally built bundles have been observed, and whether the released DMG reproduces decides `minor` vs `critical`. Incidental finding from the 44-08 live gate, deliberately NOT folded into phase 45. See `.planning/todos/pending/2026-09-17-packaged-app-renders-blank-on-roughly-one-launch-in-four.md`.
- **UPDATE (2026-09-23, live gate run, todo stays `major`/`ready: live-gate`): the blank launch is an UNMOUNT, and two premises of the 2026-09-17 entry above are REFUTED.** Probe built and landed (`src/frontend/blankRenderProbe.ts`, imported from `index.tsx`), then 39 launches of a correctly signed release-shaped bundle across six arms (13 warm repeat / 5 `open -g` background-created / 9 first-launch of a never-seen `ditto` copy / 5 under full CPU load / 3 display-asleep-through-boot / 4 both) produced **1 blank, not the reported 1 in 4** -- and that one carries its geometry: `#root` is `1280.00x0.00` with NO children and no `.App` at t+500ms through t+6000ms, region stddev 0.00, window frontmost. But the SAME log has `[Frontend]: [refreshLibrary] runner=all origin=mount` and `Frontend Ready` one second EARLIER, both from `GlobalState.componentDidMount` -- so React committed a tree and the tree was then REMOVED. Not layout, not paint, not a failure to mount. REFUTED: (1) "`#root` was populated" -- `bootErrorSurface.ts:62` runs ONLY from the error/rejection handlers, so on a launch that throws nothing it never runs and its silence said nothing about `#root`; (2) "58 MB RSS means never laid out at a paintable size" -- attributing RSS by pid-set difference (a bare `grep WebContent` matches ~16 processes owned by OTHER apps), GameLib's own WebContent on four FULLY RENDERED launches measured 44.1 / 60.6 / 79.2 / 99.1 MB. The `App.css` grid suspicion is dead either way: the F-10 guard is already in place and on the blank launch there is no `.App` to converge. NOT established: why the tree was removed (uncaught render error vs a suspension raised above the `<Suspense>` boundary -- `GlobalState`/`I18nextProvider` sit outside it and react-i18next runs `useSuspense: true`), and no error reached the log because the only paths were an invisible post-mount `console.error` and a `logError` that never sees a rejection. The probe now forwards errors AND rejections and logs `ROOT-EMPTIED` from a `MutationObserver` on `#root`, so the NEXT occurrence names its own mechanism. See `.planning/debug/packaged-blank-render.md`.
- **FIXED (2026-09-23, same session, todo downgraded to `minor`/`ready: live-gate` pending one quiet release cycle): the blank packaged launch was the DATA ROUTER rendering its initial-load state as NOTHING.** `App()` rendered `<RouterProvider router={router} />` with **no `fallbackElement`**; every route module sits behind `lazy:` (`makeLazyFunc`), and while the router resolves the FIRST one it renders `fallbackElement` -- `null` when absent. Every route element lives INSIDE the router, including the `Root` that owns `<div className="App">`, so `#root` was empty for that whole window. Named by logging the MutationObserver's own record, 3 of 3 launches identical: `removed=[div.UpdateComponent] added=[] sameContainer=true`, then `+250ms first=div#app.App`. FIX: `fallbackElement={<Loading />}` plus a 20s bound (`ROUTE_MODULE_TIMEOUT_MS`) on the route-module wait so a module that never settles reaches the existing `errorElement` instead of hanging invisibly. MEASURED: `ROOT-EMPTIED` **0 of 10** launches after, against **10 of 10** on each of TWO refuted fixes -- `withTranslation()` on `GlobalState` (suspending above the boundary) and `useSuspense: false` on the fallback pair (suspending fallback). Both were implemented, built, measured and REVERTED; both are plausible documented React behaviours that explain the symptom and both were wrong, which is the lesson: ask the DOM what changed (`removedNodes`/`addedNodes`) rather than which theory fits. Gated by `src/frontend/__tests__/routerInitialLoadFallback.test.ts`, both halves revert-to-red proven. Session closed at `.planning/debug/resolved/packaged-blank-render.md`.

- Windows packaged build breaks on darwin runner symlinks (2026-09-22, `2026-09-22-windows-packaged-build-breaks-on-darwin-runner-symlinks.md`, major): tar extracts `Python.framework` dir links as Windows FILE symlinks, so vite `copyDir` aborts; `preserveRunnerSymlinks` `symlinkSync` has no type, so it writes dangling file links into `build/` that poison the next build; and closeBundle guards mask the first error (`0 modules transformed`). Blocks every Windows packaged build and the Windows release leg. Best fix: stop fetching/copying darwin runners on non-darwin builds.

- **NEW (2026-09-23, major, `ready: code`): `checkNintendo` trusts Chromium's `standard` mapping without ever checking it, so a non-standard Nintendo pad gets all four face buttons wrong and a dead d-pad** (`2026-09-23-checknintendo-trusts-standard-mapping-on-non-standard-pads.md`). Found LIVE during the Phase 38 controller sitting on the Windows machine with a PowerA Advantage Wired Controller for Nintendo Switch 2. DETECTION IS NOT THE BUG -- `isNintendoControllerId` returns TRUE for the real id and `detectControllerLayout` correctly returns `'nintendo'`; the fault is that `gamepad.ts:578` dispatches on the id ALONE and `checkNintendo` then hard-codes `[B, A, Y, X]` standard POSITIONS. This pad reports `mapping: ""`, so Chromium passes raw HID through and the caps arrive as `[Y, B, A, X]`: physical A LAUNCHES the game while the hint bar says "A: Game details", B opens details while the bar says "B: Back", Y goes back, X opens the menu. Every glyph contradicts its button -- the exact disagreement `nintendo.ts`'s own header calls "the original defect this whole layout exists to fix". The d-pad is dead besides, arriving as a hat axis (`axes[9]`) rather than `buttons[12-15]`. **It contaminated a live measurement**, which is half the severity: it blocked Phase 38's controller leg, leaving `38-C03`/`38-C04` unscoreable on shifted indices and splitting `38-C01` into a passing stick half and a failing d-pad half. `38-C02`/`C05`/`C06`/`C08` ride on `axes[0-3]` and remain scoreable.

- **NEW (2026-09-23, major, `ready: code`): the Steam install-options CARET opens roughly 1 click in 10** (`2026-09-23-steam-install-caret-dropdown-closes-itself-via-synthetic-tab.md`). `Dropdown.toggle()` dispatches a synthetic `gamepadAction({action:'tab'})` BEFORE `setIsExpanded(true)` commits, so the Tab lands while the dropdown is still `collapsed`; `getFocusableElements()` drops zero-area nodes, focus escapes the container, and the container's own `onBlur` slams it shut in the same interaction. CLEANLY ISOLATED -- the `GameCard` context-menu door reaches the identical dialog reliably (38-S06 passed through it), so the dialog and its gating are fine. Hypothesis from source, NOT instrumented. Contaminated a measurement: `38-C08` asks whether this caret is CONTROLLER-reachable, unanswerable while the mouse cannot open it. `Dropdown` is SHARED with the NavShell tier-2 filter dropdowns, so check `38-C06`'s surface for the same fault.

- **NEW (2026-09-23, major, `ready: code`): a contiguous block of library cards renders blank art FOREVER, starting ~3.5 rows down** (`2026-09-23-library-card-art-never-recovers-from-a-missed-visible-cards-event.md`). The `visible-cards` handshake is one-shot: `GamesList` calls `observer.unobserve()` and fires a fire-and-forget `CustomEvent`, so a card whose listener was not yet attached is never told again and `GamesList`'s effect only re-runs on `library` IDENTITY change. The ~3.5-row boundary is the tell -- it is a RENDER/COMMIT boundary inside the observer's single `rootMargin: '500px'` initial batch, not a viewport boundary, which yields exactly the observed three-way split (early rows fine / blank block / everything below fine on scroll). Falsifiable: changing `rootMargin` should move the block's extent. DISTINCT from the `51b175d74` hydration race, which is about the library COUNT, not artwork -- they may share a path, but that is a question, not an established link.
- **NEW (2026-09-23, minor, `ready: code`): the install-dialog free-space line labels ONE quantity but renders TWO figures** (`2026-09-23-free-space-line-shows-two-unlabelled-figures.md`). It reads `Space Available: 301.44 GiB / 537.15 GiB`, where only the FIRST figure is available space -- the second is total disk size, unlabelled and with its relationship unstated. Found live on Windows during Phase 38 sitting 2 when the operator could not tell what the second number was. The figures are CORRECT (verified against `Win32_LogicalDisk`); this is presentation only. BOTH stores affected via the shared `message` built at `shellFilesFlowRegistration.ts:333` -- Steam dialog OBSERVED, `DownloadDialog` SOURCE-READ ONLY. Revealed, not caused, by quick `260923-o2s`: the line was previously suppressed on Windows entirely because `validPath` was false.

Wired into BOTH WR-08 guards, with the ordering constraint documented inline: raw strings must be stripped from the FULL source BEFORE `.split('\n')`, since a per-line pass cannot see a multi-line construct — reversing those two calls silently reverts the fix. | 260815-k25 | Stop AppKit painting the native macOS window title over the nav tab strip, WITHOUT blanking the window's OS-level name. **Root cause (traced to installed crate sources, and it falsified a common assumption): `TitleBarStyle::Overlay` does NOT hide the title.** In tauri-runtime-wry 2.11.4 both the creation path (`src/lib.rs:1211-1214`) and the runtime `SetTitleBarStyle` handler (`:3653-3656`) set ONLY `titlebar_transparent(true)` + `fullsize_content_view(true)`; neither touches title visibility. Title painting is an INDEPENDENT knob — `hidden_title` → `with_title_hidden` (`:1232-1235`) → `ns_window.setTitleVisibility(Hidden)` (`tao-0.35.3/src/platform_impl/macos/window.rs:269-271`), applied ONLY at window creation, which is exactly why it survives frameless toggles. Live proof: `Humankind.app/Contents/MacOS/Humankind` begins `cafebabe 00000002 01000007 00000003 00004000` — first slice at **16384**, 4x past the probe. Fix: `isExecutableMachO` replaced by a pure `classifyMachOProbe` returning a `MachOProbeVerdict` discriminated union (`executable`/`declined`/`slice`), with the caller issuing ONE bounded 32-byte positional read at the slice offset on its already-open FileHandle — deliberately NOT a bigger constant, since a slice offset is arbitrary and file-dependent. Untrusted `fat_arch.offset` bounded three ways before any I/O: structurally (`nfatArch` in [1,32], offset past its own arch table), absolute 64 MiB cap, and against real file size via `handle.stat()`; short reads decline; slice classification is non-recursive so nested fat magic cannot loop. Free side effect: `0xcafebabe` is also the Java `.class` magic, and the `nfatArch` bound declines those structurally. `MACHO_PROBE_BYTES` stays 4096. The operator was shown both readings (in-app modal vs. porting Steam's calls onto the `LOGIN_WINDOW_EVENTS` seam to earn a native window) and chose the modal; **the native-child-window reading remains UNBUILT** and is the option to revisit if true OS-window parity is ever wanted. **The first human gate then FAILED** — operator reported "steam window has sharp corners, humble rounded" and "steam window opens instantly". **Both symptoms had ONE root cause, pre-existing at HEAD and affecting all 25 Dialog consumers: `Dialog/index.css`'s `.Dialog__element` rule is DEAD CSS.** It specifies `border-radius: 10px` and a 500ms `translateY(50px)` entrance, but no element in the MUI-based primitive ever carries that class — the caller's `className` goes to `PaperProps`, and the only other mention is an inert `& .Dialog__element` DESCENDANT selector in `Dialog.tsx`'s `sx`. So every dialog in the app silently fell back to MUI's default 4px radius and default `Fade`. A class census confirmed the whole stylesheet is dead except `.Dialog__footer`; `.Dialog__input` is applied by `RedeemSteamKeyDialog` with no rule to match. **The dead rule could NOT simply be switched on:** it bases `opacity: 0`/`translateY(50px)` and restores them only under `:popover-open`/`[open]` — native `<dialog>`/popover states that can never match MUI's Paper `<div>` — so applying that class literally would have rendered EVERY DIALOG IN THE APP PERMANENTLY INVISIBLE. Operator directed "fix the primitive properly for all of them", revoking an earlier Steam-scoped fix (removed). Round 3 (`1b7fa0eaa`) therefore wires the intent through MUI's own supported mechanisms instead: `StyledPaper` gains `borderRadius: '10px'` (same `styled(Paper)` override already used for `backgroundColor`, so it does not race emotion's injected class on specificity or injection order), and `MuiDialog` gains a `Slide direction="up"` entrance at `transitionDuration={500}` via a `forwardRef` wrapper — `direction` cannot ride on `TransitionProps`, which is the bare react-transition-group type. The inert `sx` `maxWidth`/`paddingTop` pair was **deliberately DROPPED, not revived** — reviving an unreviewed `min(700px, 85vw)` would resize all 25 consumers as a side effect of a corners fix. No double backdrop introduced (`::backdrop` and the `100vmax` fake-backdrop hack are inert on a div and were not carried forward); gamepad hooks (`.MuiDialog-paper`, `.MuiDialog-root`, and the mount-time `gamepadAction` tab hack) verified unaffected against MUI source. (c) `require.resolve('eslint/bin/eslint.js')` throws `ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED` on eslint 9.29.0, so the runner uses the ESLint **Node API** -- no shell, no `spawnSync`, no exit code to lose, sidestepping this repo's whole recorded catalogue of swallow-the-failure shapes rather than dodging them one at a time.
